limitations: Deep crash/substitution tests use internal fixture roots; public installation/management and ledger flow use OS account defaults in an isolated synthetic account
Public actor names and lifecycle JSON are fixture inputs; wire-adapter proof does not establish real provider loading, trust, model-visible context or consumption
Only x86-64 Linux/WSL ext4 with Landlock ABI3+, statx birth times and procfs was exercised
Kernel null sink and preopened output buffers are deliberate exceptions to the ledger-file write set
Filesystem policy is not a hostile-code sandbox: reads, network and metadata operations are outside its scope
Creation time strengthens inode-reuse detection but is not a unique generation nonce
Physical power-loss durability and first-acquisition same-account namespace replacement are not proved
Release digests provide integrity and exact selection, not independent publisher authentication; reviewed bootstrap remains the initial trust root
Disabling only removes the command selector; it does not purge releases, alter hooks or stop in-flight workers
Inspection is a bounded best-effort observation, not an atomic snapshot, publisher authentication or authorization to retry
Native Codex trust, model-visible context, real-agent demo, native Windows proof and public release remain open; invocation-only arguments avoid persistent provider setting installation/removal
Installed-code uninstall retains non-code lock/receipt metadata and never removes provider configuration, stops workers or deletes project data; full metadata purge is unsupported
Uninstall trusts the OS account and cooperating management lock; final uncooperative same-account check-to-unlink substitution is not prevented
Corrupt/partial uninstall receipt publication can block automated retry before code deletion; no general repair/purge or automatic metadata pruning is claimed
The no-account actors and duplicate wakes are scripted: actual processes, Git/CLI/test/SQLite outcomes are proven, not real provider behavior or wake transport
SQL-readonly queries may update held WAL/SHM reader-coordination objects; no byte-for-byte no-write guarantee is made for sidecars
The strict 327-test suite does not invoke native providers; separate source-bound native discovery/startup receipts are in native-codex-discovery-result.json and native-claude-startup-result.json

Publication auditing is heuristic over selected immutable UTF-8 blobs and reachable commit metadata only, under trusted repository Git configuration/storage; it does not scan historical blobs, authenticate its executing bytes, create an export or authorize publication

External recovery requires a separately trusted bootstrap, reviewed compatible bundle, safe existing installation root and recognized selector; no fetch, root rebuild, backup restore, ledger repair or provider reauthorization is performed
Partial/damaged same-digest destinations stay blocked and preserved; a separately reviewed distinct release identity is required instead of overwrite; commands already running are not stopped

The public external-recovery fixture verifies work.intent plus claim preservation, not a new handoff/ACK scenario; both fixture version labels use the current code, not a cross-version schema migration
Six older native/public receipts and the private export receipt retain historical tested hashes; this changed runtime was not re-run through native providers or the old frozen export fixture
Rebind requires an initialized main checkout moved with the same physical Git/state/DB/WAL/SHM objects; copy, cross-filesystem migration, backup restore and account migration remain unsupported
Quiescence is an explicit operator acknowledgement, not a process stop or proven fence; cooperating rebind locks do not retroactively stop old workers or undo committed writes
Guarded binding admission requires the current compatible runtime; legacy binaries cannot enforce unknown records and manual full-account metadata/code rollback is unsupported
Rebind preserves all unknown/partial evidence; a pinned successor cannot be redirected, and malformed/conflicting/incomplete history requires diagnosis rather than automatic repair or pruning
Rebind bounds each enrollment to 128 transitions, registry inventory to 4096 entries and each JSON record to 8192 bytes; bounds fail closed and no automatic pruning is provided
Linked worktree Git pointers must be explicitly maintained/repaired with Git; existing provider invocation arguments and sessions are not rewritten
The intermediate 322-test pass missed the reproduced prepared-source edge case and was not accepted; this receipt is bound to the corrected source and 327-test run
